items.name: kimi k3
items.reason: Open-weight 2.8T MoE with strong coding and agent benchmarks, and a 1M context window.

github.readme:
What is it?

Kimi K3 is Moonshot AI’s open-weight multimodal agentic model for coding, reasoning, research, and knowledge work.

Problem solved

It targets repository-scale coding, terminal operation, and long-horizon tool use.

How does it work?

The 2.8T-parameter, 93-layer MoE activates 104B parameters, routing tokens to 16 of 896 experts.

Who should use it?

AI engineers, researchers, and teams building coding agents or long-context assistants.

Why is it useful?

A 1,048,576-token context supports repository-scale work, while sparse activation limits per-token compute.

Key capabilities

Supports Transformers, vLLM, SGLang, TokenSpeed, Kimi Code CLI, and OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible APIs.

Performance

At maximum effort, K3 reports 93.5 on GPQA Diamond, 88.3 on Terminal-Bench 2.1, and 91.2 on BrowseComp.

Maturity/status

Full weights and a hosted API are available.

huggingface.readme:
What is it?

Kimi K3 is Moonshot AI’s open-weight native multimodal agentic model.

Problem solved

Long-running coding, research, and tool workflows with limited oversight.

How does it work?

2.8T MoE, 104B active, 93 layers, MXFP4 weights and MXFP8 activations.

Who should use it?

AI engineers and researchers building coding or multimodal agents.

Why is it useful?

Sparse activation and a 1,048,576-token context.

Key capabilities

Text and images, optional video understanding, vLLM, SGLang, OpenAI/Anthropic APIs.

Performance

93.5 GPQA Diamond, 88.3 Terminal-Bench 2.1, 94.5 MCPMark-Verified, 91.1 OmniDocBench.

items.name: Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1
items.reason: Unified 7B image generation and editing model with RGBA output and multi-reference control.

github.description: Qwen-Image is a powerful and native multimodal image generation model.
github.readme:
What is it?

Qwen-Image is the official GitHub project for Qwen image generation and editing models.

Problem solved

It unifies text-to-image generation, image editing, and transparent asset workflows.

How does it work?

Diffusers pipelines expose QwenImage21Pipeline with mixed-granularity attention.

Who should use it?

Developers building image-generation or editing applications.

Why is it useful?

One checkpoint covers RGB, RGBA, identity preservation, and local edits.

Key capabilities

Up to 10 reference images, mask-based local edits, and high-resolution output.

Performance

Documented resolutions include 2048×2048 and 16:9 up to 2752×1536.

huggingface.readme:
What is it?

Qwen-Image-2.1 is a unified text-to-image generation and image-editing model.

Problem solved

It consolidates generation, localized editing, subject extraction, and transparency.

How does it work?

The visual generator has 7B parameters and 32 Single-Stream DiT layers.

Who should use it?

AI engineers building image-generation or editing applications.

Why is it useful?

Native alpha-channel output and high-resolution generation.

Key capabilities

Up to 10 reference images, local edits, identity preservation, and RGBA assets.

Performance

Recommended resolutions include 2048×2048, 2752×1536, and 1536×2752.

items.name: alibaba/open-code-review
items.reason: Production-scale hybrid code-review CLI with line-level comments and strong precision on AACR-Bench.

github.description: Hybrid architecture code review tool: deterministic pipelines + LLM Agent, precise line-level comments.
github.readme:
What is it?

OpenCodeReview is Alibaba’s open-source AI code-review CLI.

Problem solved

It targets missed files, drifting comment locations, and noisy agent reviews.

How does it work?

Deterministic pipelines handle file selection, bundling, rules, and positioning; an LLM agent retrieves context.

Who should use it?

Developers and teams reviewing changes or automating CI/CD review.

Why is it useful?

Higher precision and about one-ninth the tokens versus a general-purpose agent on the same model.

Key capabilities

Workspace, range, commit, and scan modes; MCP; GitHub Actions; GitLab CI; Gerrit.

Performance

AACR-Bench: 50 repositories, 200 PRs, 10 languages, 1,505 issues.

Maturity/status

Internal version served tens of thousands of developers for two years before open-sourcing.

items.name: prism-ml/Ternary-Bonsai-2-27B-gguf
items.reason: 27B ternary GGUF that keeps most FP16 quality at about 6GB for local deployment.

github.description: llama.cpp fork with TurboQuant and PrismML Ternary-Bonsai-27B GGUF support.
github.readme:
What is it?

A CUDA llama.cpp fork adding TurboQuant and PrismML Bonsai 27B Q1_0 / ternary Q2_0 GGUF formats.

Problem solved

It reduces model and KV-cache memory for local long-context GPU inference.

How does it work?

TurboQuant uses Walsh–Hadamard transforms, Lloyd–Max quantization, and QJL correction.

Who should use it?

CUDA inference engineers and quantization researchers.

Why is it useful?

Million-token contexts without requantizing native FP4/FP8 checkpoints.

Key capabilities

Prebuilt binaries for V100, A100, RTX 4090/5090, H100, and DGX Spark.

Performance

DeepSeek-V4-Flash Q4 reached 16.5 tok/s at 1,048,576 tokens with a 9.6 GB TBQ3 cache.

Maturity/status

Development is discontinued and archived.

huggingface.readme:
What is it?

Prism ML’s Ternary Bonsai 2 27B is a 27.36B-parameter GGUF model derived from Qwen3.8-27B.

Problem solved

It puts 27B-class reasoning on laptops or one GPU.

How does it work?

Ternary {-1,0,+1} g128 weights; PTQ1_0 is 5.95 GB at 1.75 bits/weight.

Who should use it?

AI engineers deploying local agents or privacy-sensitive teams.

Why is it useful?

It shrinks a ~54 GB FP16 model to 5.95 GB while retaining reported reasoning quality.

Key capabilities

Thinking mode, coding, tool calling, optional vision via mmproj; custom llama.cpp fork required.

Performance

Averaged 84.78 vs FP16 86.32 (98.2%) across 14 thinking benchmarks; 129.9 tok/s on RTX 5090.

items.name: XingChen-AGI/Xing4.0-29B-A4B
items.reason: 29B/4B-active long-context MoE with coding and agent scores that are useful to practitioners.

huggingface.readme:
What is it?

Xing4.0-29B-A4B is China Telecom’s text-generation MoE, 29B total / 4B active, 256K context extensible to 512K.

Problem solved

Long-context engineering, tool use, coding, and domain adaptation.

How does it work?

40-layer mHC + MLA + MTP architecture, 64 routed experts, four active per token.

Who should use it?

Engineers building agents or specialized QA and contract-audit systems.

Why is it useful?

Sparse activation limits per-token compute while long context supports extended agent runs.

Key capabilities

Transformers, vLLM, SGLang, OpenAI-compatible API, LLaMA-Factory, MindFormers.

Performance

IFBench 69.67, AIME2026 90.00, SWE-bench Verified 75.00, Terminal-Bench 2.1 57.50.

items.name: Edge0/Audio8-ASR-Infinite
items.reason: Streaming bilingual ASR with constant-memory long sessions and competitive CER/WER.

huggingface.readme:
What is it?

Audio8 ASR Infinite is a native-streaming Chinese-English ASR model.

Problem solved

Responsive 24/7 transcription without memory or latency growing over long sessions.

How does it work?

A Voxtral Realtime 4B audio tower plus a Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct decoder, with rolling KV cache.

Who should use it?

Engineers building bilingual long-running speech services.

Why is it useful?

Selectable clocks and delays balance cost and accuracy.

Key capabilities

16 kHz mono audio, semantic VAD, Transformers simulated streaming, WebSocket serving.

Performance

At 80 ms/480 ms, AISHELL-1 CER 1.750% and LibriSpeech test-clean WER 3.042%.

Maturity/status

Preview ASR-base release.

items.name: obra/superpowers
items.reason: Very high 30-day GitHub growth and developer interest, useful as a tooling story.

github.description: An agentic skills framework for coding agents.
github.readme:
What is it?

Superpowers is an open skills framework for coding agents.

Problem solved

It packages reusable agent skills so coding agents can follow consistent workflows.

How does it work?

Skills are files and prompts that an agent loads to perform specialized tasks.

Who should use it?

Developers customizing Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or similar agents.

Why is it useful?

A shared skill format reduces one-off prompt engineering.

Key capabilities

Composable skills, agent-compatible layout, and community-contributed workflows.

Maturity/status

Fast-growing open-source project.
